expectedText:
SWIMMING POOL SAFETY ACT — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Pool Construction, Inc.

SWIMMING POOL SAFETY ACT INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet concerns the property at 123 Main St, Springfield, where Jordan Alex Lee ("Homeowner") is having a swimming pool or spa built or remodeled by Acme Pool Construction, Inc. ("Contractor"). It describes California's Swimming Pool Safety Act, a set of Health & Safety Code sections that attach drowning-prevention safety-feature requirements to the issuance of a building permit for new residential pool or spa construction, or for remodeling an existing one, at a private single-family home.

STATUTORY DEFINITIONS: "SWIMMING POOL" AND "ENCLOSURE"
For purposes of the Swimming Pool Safety Act, a "swimming pool" or "pool" is any structure intended for swimming or recreational bathing that contains water over 18 inches deep, a definition broad enough to include in-ground and aboveground structures, hot tubs, spas, portable spas, and nonportable wading pools. An "enclosure" is a fence, wall, or other barrier that isolates a swimming pool from access to the home.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "“Swimming pool” or “pool” means any structure intended for swimming or recreational bathing that contains water over 18 inches deep. “Swimming pool” includes in-ground and aboveground structures and includes, but is not limited to, hot tubs, spas, portable spas, and nonportable wading pools."
  — Health & Safety Code, definition of "swimming pool", Health & Safety Code § 115921(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115921.)
  "“Enclosure” means a fence, wall, or other barrier that isolates a swimming pool from access to the home."
  — Health & Safety Code, definition of "enclosure", Health & Safety Code § 115921(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115921.)
  Known gap: These definitions are drawn from the article's own definitions section and apply only "as used in this article" (Health & Safety Code § 115921) — they are not necessarily the same definitions a local building or zoning ordinance uses for permitting purposes, and they are not the definitions used in the separate part of the Health & Safety Code governing public swimming pool sanitation and design (a different article this clause set does not document). The source HTML renders the space after each subdivision letter — e.g., between "(a)" and the following word — as a non-breaking space rather than an ordinary space; this artifact was identical across two independently fetched copies of the page (different User-Agent strings) and has been normalized to an ordinary space in the quotations below.

THE PERMIT-TRIGGERED REQUIREMENT: AT LEAST TWO OF SEVEN DROWNING PREVENTION SAFETY FEATURES
When a building permit is issued for construction of a new swimming pool or spa, or for remodeling an existing one, at a private single-family home, the pool or spa must be equipped with at least two of seven listed drowning prevention safety features. The first four are: (1) an enclosure meeting the separate structural standards described elsewhere in this article; (2) removable mesh fencing meeting a specified ASTM International standard, paired with a self-closing, self-latching, key-lockable gate; (3) a manually or power-operated safety pool cover meeting a specified ASTM standard; and (4) exit alarms on doors and windows that provide direct, unenclosed access to the pool or spa, which must sound an audible alarm or repeating verbal warning when opened or left ajar.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "(a) Except as provided in Section 115925, subject to subdivision (b), and consistent with Section 1596.814, when a building permit is issued for the construction of a new swimming pool or spa or the remodeling of an existing swimming pool or spa at a private single-family home, the respective swimming pool or spa shall be equipped with at least two of the following seven drowning prevention safety features:(1) An enclosure that meets the requirements of Section 115923 and isolates the swimming pool or spa from the private single-family home.(2) Removable mesh fencing that meets the ASTM International F2286 standard in conjunction with a gate that is self-closing and self-latching and can accommodate a key lockable device.(3) A manually operated or power-operated safety pool cover that is accompanied by a label verifying that the cover meets the specifications of the ASTM International F1346-23 standard.(4) Exit alarms on the private single-family home’s doors and windows that provide direct access to the swimming pool or spa without any intervening enclosure. Whenever any door or window is opened or left ajar, exit alarms shall make either an audible, continuous alarm sound or a repeating verbal warning, such as a notification that “the door to the pool is open.” An exit alarm may be battery operated or connected to the electrical wiring of the building."
  — Health & Safety Code, two-of-seven safety feature requirement (features 1-4), Health & Safety Code § 115922(a), (a)(1)-(4) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115922.)
  Known gap: The requirement is triggered by permit issuance, not by pool ownership generally — the statute applies "when a building permit is issued for the construction of a new swimming pool or spa or the remodeling of an existing swimming pool or spa," so an older pool that predates this requirement and has not since been remodeled under a new permit is not, by this section alone, shown to be out of compliance. The source HTML wraps a mid-sentence line break (rendered as a newline followed by several tab characters) in the middle of item (2), between "can accommodate" and "a key lockable device" — identical across two independently fetched copies of the page (different User-Agent strings) — which has been normalized to a single space in the quotation below.

FEATURES FIVE THROUGH SEVEN, BARRED COMBINATIONS, AND FINAL INSPECTION
The remaining three qualifying features are: (5) a self-closing, self-latching door device with a release mechanism at least 54 inches above the floor; (6) a submersion-detection alarm in the pool or spa itself, certified to a specified ASTM standard, which does not include a wearable child alarm; and (7) a catch-all for other protective means independently verified as providing equal or greater protection under recognized standards. The statute then bars three specific combinations from being counted as two separate qualifying features: an exit alarm paired with a self-closing, self-latching device on the same door; an exit alarm paired with a door latch on separate doors; and a safety pool cover paired with a submersion-detection alarm. Before final approval of the permitted construction or remodeling work, the local building code official must inspect the drowning-prevention safety features and, finding no violations, give final approval.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "(5) A self-closing, self-latching device with a release mechanism placed no lower than 54 inches above the floor on the private single-family home’s doors providing direct access to the swimming pool or spa.(6) An alarm in good repair and operable as designed that, when placed in a swimming pool or spa, will sound upon detection of accidental or unauthorized entrance into the water. The alarm shall meet and be independently certified to the ASTM International F2208 standard that includes surface motion, pressure, sonar, laser, and infrared type alarms. A swimming protection alarm feature designed for individual use, including an alarm attached to a child that sounds when the child exceeds a certain distance or becomes submerged in water, is not a qualifying drowning prevention safety feature.(7) Other means of protection, if the degree of protection afforded is equal to or greater than that afforded by any of the features set forth above and has been independently verified by an approved testing laboratory as meeting standards for those features established by ASTM International, the American Society of Mechanical Engineers, or another nationally recognized standards development organization, and the feature is accompanied by a label verifying that the protection meets those standards.(b) The requirements of subdivision (a) are not satisfied by any of the following:(1) An exit alarm and a self-closing, self-latching device on the same door.(2) An exit alarm and a door latch on separate doors.(3) A safety pool cover and an alarm described in paragraph (6) of subdivision (a).(c) Before the issuance of a final approval for the completion of permitted construction or remodeling work, the local building code official shall inspect the drowning safety prevention features required by this section and, if no violations are found, shall give final approval."
  — Health & Safety Code, two-of-seven safety feature requirement (features 5-7), barred combinations, and final inspection, Health & Safety Code § 115922(a)(5)-(7), (b), (c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115922.)
  Known gap: The barred-combination list in subdivision (b) is a closed list of three specific pairings — it does not generally forbid counting any two installed features toward the two-feature minimum, even where they physically overlap in some way; a combination not named in subdivision (b) (such as an enclosure paired with a pool cover) is not shown to be barred by this text. Compliance is verified by inspection from "the local building code official" — a local, not a state, official — tying enforcement of this state statute to local permitting administration. The source HTML wraps mid-sentence line breaks (rendered as a newline followed by several tab characters) twice within this span — within item (5), between "private single-family home’s doors" and "providing direct access," and within item (7), between "as meeting standards for" and "those features established" — identical across two independently fetched copies of the page (different User-Agent strings) — both normalized to a single space in the quotation below.

STRUCTURAL SPECIFICATIONS FOR AN ENCLOSURE CHOSEN AS A QUALIFYING FEATURE
If the enclosure feature is one of the two qualifying features selected, the enclosure must meet five structural specifications: access gates open away from the pool and are self-closing and self-latching with the latch no lower than 60 inches above the ground; the enclosure is at least 60 inches high; the maximum vertical clearance between the ground and the bottom of the enclosure is two inches; any gaps or voids do not allow passage of a sphere four inches or more in diameter; and the outside surface is free of protrusions, cavities, or other features that could let a child under five climb over it.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "An enclosure shall have all of the following characteristics:(a) Any access gates through the enclosure open away from the swimming pool, and are self-closing with a self-latching device placed no lower than 60 inches above the ground. (b) A minimum height of 60 inches. (c) A maximum vertical clearance from the ground to the bottom of the enclosure of two inches. (d) Gaps or voids, if any, do not allow passage of a sphere equal to or greater than four inches in diameter. (e) An outside surface free of protrusions, cavities, or other physical characteristics that would serve as handholds or footholds that could enable a child below the age of five years to climb over."
  — Health & Safety Code, structural characteristics of a qualifying enclosure, Health & Safety Code § 115923 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115923.)
  Known gap: These structural specifications apply specifically to an "enclosure" chosen under item (1) of the two-of-seven list; if a homeowner instead selects two of the other six listed features (for example, a pool cover and exit alarms), these particular dimensional specifications for fences and gates do not apply to what is actually installed. The source HTML inserts a non-breaking space after each subdivision letter (e.g., between "(a)" and the following word) and wraps a mid-sentence line break (a newline followed by several tab characters) within subdivision (c), between "enclosure of two" and "inches" — both identical across two independently fetched copies of the page (different User-Agent strings) — and both have been normalized to a single ordinary space in the quotation below.

WHAT THE SWIMMING POOL SAFETY ACT DOES NOT COVER
The Swimming Pool Safety Act's requirements do not apply to public swimming pools; hot tubs or spas equipped with locking safety covers that comply with a specified ASTM International standard; or an apartment complex, or any residential setting other than a single-family home.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "The requirements of this article do not apply to any of the following:(a) Public swimming pools.(b) Hot tubs or spas with locking safety covers that comply with the ASTM International F1346 standard.(c) An apartment complex, or any residential setting other than a single-family home."
  — Health & Safety Code, exemptions from the Swimming Pool Safety Act, Health & Safety Code § 115925 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115925.)
  Known gap: The third exemption removes multi-family rental housing pools from this article entirely — a pool at an apartment complex is not subject to the two-of-seven-features permit requirement documented in this clause set at all, though it may be separately regulated as a "public swimming pool" under a different part of the Health & Safety Code that this clause set does not document. The hot tub/spa exemption in subdivision (b) is narrow: it requires a locking safety cover that specifically complies with the named ASTM standard, not merely any cover.

STATE AGENCIES ARE BARRED FROM REINTERPRETING THIS ARTICLE; TWO SPECIFIC POINTS ARE RESERVED TO LOCAL JURISDICTIONS
The Swimming Pool Safety Act is not subject to further modification or interpretation by any state regulatory agency; that authority is instead reserved exclusively to local jurisdictions, specifically as to the catch-all "other means of protection" feature and the apartment-complex/non-single-family exemption.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, this article shall not be subject to further modification or interpretation by any regulatory agency of the state, this authority being reserved exclusively to local jurisdictions, as provided for in paragraph (7) of subdivision (a) of Section 115922 and subdivision (c) of Section 115925."
  — Health & Safety Code, bar on state-agency reinterpretation; authority reserved to local jurisdictions, Health & Safety Code § 115927 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115927.)
  Known gap: This reservation is narrow and textually specific — it names only two provisions (the catch-all seventh safety feature in § 115922(a)(7) and the residential-setting exemption in § 115925(c)) as reserved to local jurisdictions; it is not a general statement that local governments control enforcement or interpretation of the article's other, more specific requirements (such as the enclosure dimensions in § 115923), and it does not itself describe what procedure a local jurisdiction must follow in exercising that reserved authority.

A CONTRACTOR'S DUTY TO GIVE NOTICE OF THE ARTICLE'S REQUIREMENTS
Anyone entering into an agreement to build a swimming pool or spa, or to perform permitted work on one covered by this article, must give the consumer notice of the article's requirements.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "(a) Any person entering into an agreement to build a swimming pool or spa, or to engage in permitted work on a pool or spa covered by this article, shall give the consumer notice of the requirements of this article."
  — Health & Safety Code, contractor's duty to notify the consumer, Health & Safety Code § 115924(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=115924.)
  Known gap: This notice duty is stated without specifying a required form, required method of delivery (written or oral), or a specific penalty within this article for a contractor's failure to give it. A separate, non-mandatory part of the same statutory section encourages pool contractors to share state-published consumer safety information and materials from named private organizations, but that is described as encouragement rather than as part of the notice duty itself, and this clause set does not document it as a separate requirement.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF RECEIPT
The undersigned acknowledge receipt of this Swimming Pool Safety Act information sheet concerning the property at 123 Main St, Springfield.

☐ _________________________ Jordan Alex Lee (Homeowner)   Date: _______________

☐ _________________________ Acme Pool Construction, Inc. (Contractor)   Date: _______________
